subject: Cross-border onboarding: DocuSign cadence & evidence runbook
messages:
From: Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@healthsync.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cross-border onboarding: initial ask and timeline

Hi Logan / team,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. To get procurement and legal to signature we need a concise plan for: SCCs/UK IDTA applicability, TIA scope (EU processing vs UK addendum), a list of subprocessors that will touch EU/UK customer data, and an anchor DocuSign window that Procurement can calendar.

Attached are our DPA redlines and our internal processing map for reference (see attachments). Can you confirm the following by Monday?
- Which standard contractual clauses (SCCs) you intend to rely on for EU customers and whether you are using the UK IDTA + UK Addendum for UK-resident data.
- A one-page evidence list for our Security team (SOC 2 + data residency assertions + logging/audit cadence).
- Proposed DocuSign signature window (start/end dates) and any staged sign approach (canary customers first).

Procurement contact is procurement@healthsync.com; they will need a DocuSign link and a brief mutual action plan (MAP).

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Schultz
Head of Legal Operations, HealthSync Ltd
attachments: HealthSync_DPA_redline_20261103.pdf; processing_map_healthsync.csv
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border onboarding: initial ask and timeline

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Below is a proposed, pragmatic plan that aligns with Redwood's standard international transfer posture.

Summary (high level)
- EU customers: We rely on the EU Commission SCCs (controller-processor flow) with our DPA.
- UK customers: We attach the UK IDTA + Redwood's UK Addendum.
- TIA/DTIA scope: We will provide a TIA for customers requiring additional technical safeguards; for HealthSync we'll include the TIA annex that documents data localization (EU region), subprocessors touching content, and KV cache/ejection policies.

Proposed DocuSign cadence (suggested MAP)
1) Week 0 (Nov 15-19): Share final DPA (we incorporate a small set of your redlines) + DocuSign envelope to Procurement for review.
2) Week 1 (Nov 22-26): Staged signature window — signatory group 1 (legal + procurement).
3) Week 2 (Nov 29-Dec 3): Signatory group 2 (business owners).
4) Week 3 (Dec 6-10): Completion and evidence handoff to Security for onboarding.

Evidence we will provide in the handoff
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), date range and controls matrix (Attachment: redline_summary.docx).
- Processing map (CSV) with region flags for all subprocessors (we will mark subprocessors that access EU/UK data).
- Export controls + retention policy excerpt and access logs sampling procedure.

Action items for HealthSync
- Confirm if you want a single global DPA or separate EU/UK attachments for signature.
- Confirm Procurement contact for the DocuSign envelope and any internal pause dates (holiday blackout for signatures).

I'll take point on the DPA redline consolidation. Marissa, Kimberly — can you add any product/infra constraints below?

Cheers,
Logan
Logan Wright
Manager, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 8, 2026 at 11:03 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Below is a proposed, pragmatic plan that aligns with Redwood's standard international transfer posture.
> 
> Summary (high level)
> - EU customers: We rely on the EU Commission SCCs (controller-processor flow) with our DPA.
> - UK customers: We attach the UK IDTA + Redwood's UK Addendum.

Adding technical confirmations from Infra:
- Data residency: For HealthSync's EU processing requirement we will pin inference workloads to the AWS eu-west-1 region and log processing region at the request level.
- Subprocessors: Current subprocessors that may access customer content are listed in the attached CSV; we will flag those with EU/UK access and provide attestations for any that do persistent logging of request metadata.
- KV cache and prefix caching: We will provide a short note describing our KV eviction and cache partitioning so your security team can validate TIA assumptions.

Timeline constraint: we will need at least 5 business days after signature to complete deployment of region-pinning and logging configurations for your production tenant. If Procurement requires a faster window, flag now so we can schedule overtime.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

Anna
